_convention.name: OBSERVABILITY.vocabulary
_convention.edits_are_lost: This file has no unmanaged region. Hand edits are overwritten on the next render; change the template in dev-agent-tools instead.
_convention.agreement: conventions check asserts that the event names here and in the prose are the SAME SET, in both directions.

security_events.closed_means: A producer MUST NOT invent a name. One app with its own spelling is one blind spot, and a blind spot nobody knows about.

common_fields.note: from the event list below, exactly
the PSEUDONYMOUS id, never a raw identifier
the source address as the app saw it
a per-session random id, never the session token itself

security_events.common_fields_note: These are in addition to the required log fields every record carries.

auth.login.success.means: a credential was accepted and a session began

additional_fields.note: A CODE, not prose, because prose cannot be counted. Legitimate in the LOG; the answer to the caller must not say which half was wrong.

auth.token.refused.means: a presented token was invalid, expired or unknown

authz.denied.means: an authenticated principal was refused an action

additional_fields.note: the permission or role that was required

authz.role.change.means: a role, group or permission was granted or removed

additional_fields.note: the user whose roles changed, pseudonymous

_deliberately_absent.note: These are NOT omissions. A consumer reading an absent key as an oversight would invent one, which is the defect this file exists to stop.

classification_rule.absent_because: Unsettled. fixloop classifies by family prefix; opscenter matches exact names. A rule encoded here before those two agree would be a guess that consumers delete their hand copies in favour of.

reserved_namespaces.absent_because: Not part of this convention. The prose contains no reserved-namespace section; the only occurrence on this box is in one consumer's own release notes, which makes it that consumer's operational concern until it is written into the prose as a versioned change.
